verses.text: From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the LORD his God,

xrefs.text: They dropped me alive into a pit and cast stones upon me.
A song of ascents. Out of the depths I cry to You, O LORD!
When he calls out to Me, I will answer him; I will be with him in trouble. I will deliver him and honor him.
Though He slay me, I will hope in Him. I will still defend my ways to His face.
O LORD, they sought You in their distress; when You disciplined them, they poured out a quiet prayer.

verses.text: saying: “In my distress I called to the LORD, and He answered me. From the belly of Sheol I called for help, and You heard my voice.

xrefs.text: The cords of death encompassed me; the torrents of chaos overwhelmed me.
A song of ascents. In my distress I cried to the LORD, and He answered me.
This poor man called out, and the LORD heard him; He saved him from all his troubles.
For great is Your loving devotion to me; You have delivered me from the depths of Sheol.
A song. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. For the choirmaster. According to Mahalath Leannoth. A Maskil of Heman the Ezrahite. O LORD, the God of my salvation, day and night I cry out before You.

verses.text: For You cast me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and the current swirled about me; all Your breakers and waves swept over me.

xrefs.text: Deep calls to deep in the roar of Your waterfalls; all Your breakers and waves have rolled over me.
The waters flowed over my head, and I thought I was going to die.
For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Lilies.” Of David. Save me, O God, for the waters are up to my neck.
I am forsaken among the dead, like the slain who lie in the grave, whom You remember no more, who are cut off from Your care.
Rescue me from the mire and do not let me sink; deliver me from my foes and out of the deep waters.

verses.text: At this, I said, ‘I have been banished from Your sight; yet I will look once more toward Your holy temple.’

xrefs.text: In my alarm I said, “I am cut off from Your sight!” But You heard my plea for mercy when I called to You for help.
But I will enter Your house by the abundance of Your loving devotion; in reverence I will bow down toward Your holy temple.

and when they return to You with all their heart and soul in the land of the enemies who took them captive, and when they pray in the direction of the land that You gave to their fathers, the city You have chosen, and the house I have built for Your Name,
Surely for my own welfare I had such great anguish; but Your love has delivered me from the pit of oblivion, for You have cast all my sins behind Your back.
And I will cast you out of My presence, just as I have cast out all your brothers, all the descendants of Ephraim.

verses.text: The waters engulfed me to take my life; the watery depths closed around me; the seaweed wrapped around my head.

xrefs.text: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Lilies.” Of David. Save me, O God, for the waters are up to my neck.
The waters flowed over my head, and I thought I was going to die.
He lifted me up from the pit of despair, out of the miry clay; He set my feet upon a rock, and made my footsteps firm.

verses.text: To the roots of the mountains I descended; the earth beneath me barred me in forever! But You raised my life from the pit, O LORD my God!

xrefs.text: O LORD, You pulled me up from Sheol; You spared me from descending into the Pit.
For You will not abandon my soul to Sheol, nor will You let Your Holy One see decay.
Surely for my own welfare I had such great anguish; but Your love has delivered me from the pit of oblivion, for You have cast all my sins behind Your back.
Answer me quickly, O LORD; my spirit fails. Do not hide Your face from me, or I will be like those who descend to the Pit.
Before the mountains were settled, before the hills, I was brought forth,

verses.text: As my life was fading away, I remembered the LORD. My prayer went up to You, to Your holy temple.

xrefs.text: In my distress I called upon the LORD; I cried to my God for help. From His temple He heard my voice, and my cry for His help reached His ears.
Then the priests and the Levites stood to bless the people, and God heard their voice, and their prayer came into His holy dwelling place in heaven.
The LORD is in His holy temple; the LORD is on His heavenly throne. His eyes are watching closely; they examine the sons of men.
I remember the days of old; I meditate on all Your works; I consider the work of Your hands.
And David was greatly distressed because the people spoke of stoning him, because the soul of every man grieved for his sons and daughters. But David found strength in the LORD his God.

verses.text: Those who cling to worthless idols forsake His loving devotion.

xrefs.text: I hate those who cling to worthless idols, but in the LORD I trust.

They rejected His statutes and the covenant He had made with their fathers, as well as the decrees He had given them. They pursued worthless idols and became worthless themselves, going after the surrounding nations that the LORD had commanded them not to imitate.
“For My people have committed two evils: They have forsaken Me, the fountain of living water, and they have dug their own cisterns— broken cisterns that cannot hold water.
Do not turn aside after worthless things that cannot profit you or deliver you, for they are empty.
But they are altogether senseless and foolish, instructed by worthless idols made of wood!

verses.text: But I, with the voice of thanksgiving, will sacrifice to You. I will fulfill what I have vowed. Salvation is from the LORD!”

xrefs.text: Salvation belongs to the LORD; may Your blessing be on Your people. Selah
Sacrifice a thank offering to God, and fulfill your vows to the Most High.
When you make a vow to God, do not delay in fulfilling it, because He takes no pleasure in fools. Fulfill your vow.
Through Jesus, therefore, let us continually offer to God a sacrifice of praise, the fruit of lips that confess His name.
He who sacrifices a thank offering honors Me, and to him who rightly orders his way, I will show the salvation of God.”

verses.text: And the LORD commanded the fish, and it vomited Jonah onto dry land.

xrefs.text: “You of little faith, Jesus replied, “why are you so afraid? Then He got up and rebuked the winds and the sea, and it was perfectly calm.
For He spoke, and it came to be; He commanded, and it stood firm.
The centurion answered, “Lord, I am not worthy to have You come under my roof. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.

Why was no one there when I arrived? Why did no one answer when I called? Is My hand too short to redeem you? Or do I lack the strength to deliver you? Behold, My rebuke dries up the sea; I turn the rivers into a desert; the fish rot for lack of water and die of thirst.
And God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.
